label: Copy phase after first output (sparse, content-dependent)
explanation: Fires exclusively in the copy phase from the second output onward (recall_idx >= 1); never in the original phase, at <DEL>, or at the first copy step. Within that window it is active on only ~13% of steps, so the predicate captures all activation mass but has low precision. Rate is highest for short sequences (L=3: 33% of steps, holding the strongest activations, top examples are L=3 at the final step) and for recall_idx 2-5 / to_go=1; it is weak for L=5-6. Some token preference (in_tok i, d, x; out_tok 0, c, x) but token sets only lift F1 to ~0.32. The remaining selectivity looks distributed/content-dependent and was not captured by any simple predicate.
